title: Your own vtable, inspected
description:
Look at the vtable of a class you wrote and match its slots to functions.

```
class Monster { virtual ~Monster(); virtual void update(); virtual int damage(); }
Goblin overrides damage
Monster vtable: slot 0 ~Monster, 1 Monster::update, 2 Monster::damage
Goblin vtable:  slot 0 ~Goblin,  1 Monster::update, 2 Goblin::damage
the first 8 bytes of a Goblin point at Goblin's table
```
hints: Two `Goblin` objects share the same vtable pointer; a `Monster` has a different one (lesson 9.06).
In the Visual Studio watch window, expanding an object shows `__vfptr` and its entries with names.
requirements: Read the vtable pointer from an object (the first pointer-sized value) and compare it between objects.
Print the slot addresses and compare them with `&Monster::update`-style information (or names from a debugger).
Note in a comment that this layout is the compiler's choice, not guaranteed by C++.
stretch: Add a second base class and look for the second vtable pointer.
